newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian govt eyes fuel tax rebate ceiling.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian govt eyes fuel tax rebate ceiling.

text.p: The Australian Government will consider imposing a ceiling on the diesel fuel tax rebate if it fails to reach an agreement with the mining industry by the end of October over changes to the programme, Resources Minister Warwick Parer told Reuters on Monday.

The rebate, worth about $700 million in fiscal 1995/96 last year, to the mining industry in 1995 was retained by the government in its latest budget although the government said the programme needed changes.
The rebate returns to off-road diesel users such as farmers and miners a long-standing tax on diesel that was introduced as a measrue to fund roads.
Outside of Australia the rebate has been criticised in some mining sectors as being an unfair form of a subsidy.
Parer earlier told a coal conference in Sydney that the rebate had grown at a compounded annual rate of about 12 percent a year over the last four years.
He said "clever lawyers" had found ways to exploit the programme.
Parer said the deadline at the end of October was needed to allow enough time for any changes to be debated in the senate.
